# SK2001 — Comparison is fixed by the integral type's range

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A relational comparison against an integral constant is always true or false over the operand type's complete range.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

Fixed-width integral types cannot represent values outside their declared ranges. Testing an endpoint can therefore be redundant even where the compiler does not issue CS0652. This initial rule uses exact ranges rather than treating nullable annotations as runtime guarantees. It reports without removing expressions that may throw or have side effects.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
bool M(byte value) => value >= 0;
```

Write:

```csharp
bool M(byte value) => value > 0; // if zero was intended to be excluded
```

## When it does not fire

Only built-in, non-lifted relational comparisons over fixed-width integral/char types and integral constants are supported. Native integers, floating point, decimal, nullable values, overloaded operators, two constant operands, and cases already reported by CS0652 are excluded. Constant dependencies must come from metadata or this source file, including transitive initializers. Flow-dependent and nullability-derived comparisons are outside this initial scope. There is no automatic fix.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2001.severity`
